title: Trails of Stars over Paranal
caption: Star trails and a laser beam over Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Long arcs of starlight curve around the south celestial pole above Paranal Observatory. An illuminated road below winds up the mountain toward the observatory, where two of the four Unit Telescopes of ESO's Very Large Telescope (VLT) and the VST stand on the summit of Cerro Paranal. An orange beacon, the laser beams from one of those Unit Telescopes, sweeps through the sky.

Pictures like this make our planet's motion visible. Earth travels around the Sun on an elliptical path, but it also spins on its axis, and that rotation makes the stars appear to shift position and wheel across the sky in long arcs.

To capture this motion, photographer Fred Kamphues took several long-exposure shots and stacked them together. The long exposure also accentuates the laser, stretching it into the broad orange sweep seen here.

understand.summary: This is a stack of several long-exposure photographs by Fred Kamphues. The source does not publish camera or color-processing details.
understand.eye: The eye sees stars as points and a laser as a thin beam. The stacked long exposures turn the stars into arcs and smear the laser into a sweeping band.
